answers.question: The race got moved two weeks earlier, to October 18, because of the bridge works. That's three weeks from today. I've only done one 20. Do I still have time for my 22-miler?
answers.answer:
No, do not add a 22-miler now. With the race on Sun Oct 18, this coming Sunday is already 2 weeks out, which is the window where a very long run costs you more than it gives: fitness from a run that long takes about 10 to 14 days to show up, and the fatigue would still be in your legs on race morning.

Here is what matters more than mileage: you have a 20 and a 17 in the last 4 weeks, both finished strong and even-paced, and your easy pace at 139 bpm is steady. That is a body that is ready. Instead of chasing one more big number, this Sunday you will run 16 mi with the last 4 at marathon pace (around 8:35/mi). That rehearses race pace on tired legs, which is the specific thing left to practice.

new.analysis:
## Why this week looks like this

You followed the plan cleanly: easy days at 138 bpm, 3 x 2 mi threshold at 7:58/mi with only a 1% fade, and 17 mi on Sunday at 9:59/mi with modest drift. That is a healthy peak week and tells me the fitness is there for sub-3:45.

The race moving up two weeks changes the shape of the block, not the fitness. We were planning a 20 next weekend and a taper after; instead this Sunday becomes a 16 with marathon-pace work, and then we taper hard. The one new piece is Wednesday: a marathon-pace session rather than threshold, because at 2 weeks out we want pace specificity, not more lactate work.

Keep the easy days truly easy, under 145 bpm, and resist the urge to "make up" for the lost build weeks. Sleep and food matter more than any extra mile from here on. Next week will drop volume meaningfully and keep a short tune-up with some race-pace running.
